text:
mina: quick heads-up, ran an nsys capture against the vllm->TensorRT wrapper on the 40B test rig, and the wrapper+scheduler overhead jumped ~1.6ms/token vs last week :thinking:
mina: full capture (50 requests, 1-32 batch sizes) uploaded: https://redwood-internal/ci/nsys/1785001234.nsys
mina: top-level observation: a lot of time is now in `vllm::tensorrt::Wrapper::dispatch` on the host, not inside TRT kernels. CPU timeline shows repeated short memcpy + kernel-launch syscall sequences with gaps about ~800-1200us between launches
igor: do you have the kernel timeline (perfetto view) or the lineage for a single long request? :eyes:
mina: pasted a trimmed perfetto view snippet below:
```
CPU: vllm wrapper lock wait  1.2ms
CPU: host memcpy H2D         0.6ms
CUDA: kernelLaunch (TRT)    0.2ms
CUDA: kernel (attention)    0.5ms
CPU: schedule next batch    0.9ms
```
mina: also saw repeated KV cache `serialize()` calls sprinkled between launches for partially-filled batches
evan: that KV serialize is suspicious. Did we change the batching heuristic recently? I remember a change that forces per-request cache flush for safety when batch < 4
mina: yeah, https://git.redwood/infra/changeset/abc123 - the heuristic now prefers latency over batching for mixed-size queues, but it seems to trigger extra memcpy/serialize churn
tara: can you grep for the mutex hotspots? in the nsys flame it looked like `Scheduler::pop` holding `queue_mutex` while calling `copy_to_device()`
mina: exactly. timeline shows `Scheduler::dispatch` holds the lock ~900-1100us while doing host->device memcpys for each sample. That serializes device transfers across workers instead of overlapping them
igor: oof. That explains single-threaded H2D tail. We should either move memcpy out of the critical section or use async pinned buffers + cudaMemcpyAsync with stream syncing outside the lock
evan: quick repro command so infra can reproduce: `./perf/run_inference_bench --model redwood/40b --concurrency 8 --seq 1024 --profile nsys --capture 50 --batch-policy mixed-latency`
evan: then open with: `nsys-ui capture.nsys` and inspect Host Trace + CUDA API timeline
mina: small data point: comparing before/after change, avg per-token CPU overhead went from 0.9ms -> 2.5ms for mixed workloads on that rig
mina: also noticed that TRT engine calls are much shorter than before because inputs are smaller, so proportionally wrapper overhead dominates now
perf-bot: perf regression alert by CI for job redwood/runtime/mixed-latency/40b: +72% host-side latency (PR #4821)
igor: can someone try a quick patch: move `copy_to_device()` out of queue_mutex and push a descriptor into a lock-free staging queue that the sender thread drains to perform async memcpy? low-risk experiment
tara: I'll prototype in a branch and run the same nsys capture
buildbot: started job: eng-runtime/batching/patch-queue-async (job id 6523)
mina: thanks. if the async memcpy reduces lock holding we should also tweak the batching heuristic to avoid forcing cache serialize for small batches (that was the second culprit)
evan: agree. proposal: only serialize KV cache on cold-starts or when we detect cross-request KV conflicts; otherwise use per-request delta-apply that is lock-free
igor: good plan. for the immediate mitigation, tara's async-memcpy + pinned-buffer path should show wall-time wins in nsys. if not, we also need to instrument `nvtxRangePush` in wrapper entry points to ensure no unexpected work hiding on CPU
tara: will update with a capture link once job finishes :party:
mina: thanks all — priority P1 for this perf regression since it affects Dedicated throughput SLOs and unit cost.
mina: tl;dr: nsys shows wrapper/scheduler lock + H2D memcpys + KV serialize causing ~1.6ms/token regression; next steps: async memcpy outside lock + tweak KV serialize heuristic
